title: Cambodian genocide under the Khmer Rouge
summary: From 17 April 1975 to 7 January 1979 the Khmer Rouge ruled Cambodia, emptying cities, forcing millions into labour in the countryside and killing officials and perceived enemies; disease and starvation spread. Estimates of deaths run from about 1.7 million (Yale Cambodian Genocide Program) to nearly two million (US Holocaust Memorial Museum). A Vietnamese invasion ended the regime.

uncertainty.note: Dates of Khmer Rouge rule as given by the US Holocaust Memorial Museum.

audience_note: Describes a genocide: forced evacuation, executions, forced labour, starvation and disease. Death-toll figures are estimates that differ by source.
